name: Strike Lab: Solo Combo Training Arena
request: Create a small, playable Strike Lab fighting-game training arena for one player on desktop and touch. Include a humanoid training dummy, a three-hit light-attack combo with visible windup, contact and recovery animations, synchronized hit sound effects, a visible accepted-hit counter and dummy health. The server must validate attack timing and range. Each accepted strike damages and counts once at contact; swinging out of range, holding the button or spamming during recovery must not create extra hits. Show distinct hit and miss feedback. After defeat, reset the dummy and let the player practice again; provide a clear reset control and an uncluttered arena. Search Marketplace first for complete reusable combat/training components, compatible dummy rigs, existing animations and sound rather than rebuilding everything. Inspect compatibility, behavior and included media, preserve useful working pieces and author only missing integration. Source missing audio from Marketplace and verify actual playing animations and audible sounds. Record an importer capability gap honestly rather than treating it as a bad asset. Choose reasonable styling and damage values yourself. No PvP, matchmaking, saving, monetization or large world. Success needs native evidence for the full combo, exact counting, misses, recovery spam, defeat/reset and desktop/touch controls. A damage script with a static dummy does not meet the animation requirement.

spec.title: Strike Lab: Solo Combo Training Arena
spec.summary:
Create a compact, single-player fighting-game practice lab centered on one server-authoritative humanoid dummy. From a safe spawn, the player immediately sees a raised octagonal training mat, the dummy at the far target mark, a concise HUD showing dummy health and accepted hits, and clearly labeled Attack and Reset controls. The short approach lane teaches spacing: attack near the dummy to land strikes, or attack from outside range to observe distinct miss feedback. Desktop uses a primary attack binding and reset key/button; touch uses large, separated on-screen Attack and Reset buttons.

The core action is a three-step light combo. Each step visibly moves through windup, contact, and recovery. A request starts an attack only when the server-authoritative sequence permits it; contact is evaluated once at a server-controlled contact time. A valid in-range contact deals damage, increments the accepted-hit counter exactly once, plays synchronized impact audio, flashes hit feedback, and causes a visible dummy reaction. An out-of-range contact produces miss feedback without damage or count changes. Holding Attack does not auto-repeat, and new requests during recovery are rejected without producing additional contacts. Reasonable defaults are 100 dummy health, combo damage of 10/12/18, a short continuation window, and a slightly stronger third-hit presentation; exact timing may be adapted to verified Marketplace animation markers while preserving clear phases and server validation.

Dummy defeat produces a brief defeated state, then automatically restores the dummy so practice can continue. The accepted-hit counter remains useful across automatic dummy restorations, while the explicit Reset control immediately restores health, clears transient combat state, and returns the accepted-hit count to zero. Character respawn also clears stale attack state and safely rebinds controls and HUD state. No PvP, matchmaking, persistence, monetization, progression system, or large explorable world is included.

Marketplace discovery and inspection precede implementation decisions. Complete combat/training systems are evaluated before replacement code, followed by compatible humanoid rigs, animation-bearing models, and audio. Useful audited behavior, rigs, animation markers, and media are preserved. Script ownership and exact glue paths remain discovery-dependent until imported hierarchies, source code, dependencies, rig compatibility, and media provenance are inspected. Standalone animation retrieval is unsupported by the current adapter, so required animation discovery targets Models containing compatible animation assets; inability to preserve or import those animations is reported as a blocking capability gap, not treated as asset failure or permission to substitute static/procedural motion.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a clean near-future sports-science lab rather than a featureless floor. The playable area is a compact rectangular room approximately 46 by 34 studs with a safe collidable spawn pad, a short illuminated approach lane, and a central octagonal training mat. Low boundary rails and wall panels communicate the arena limits without obstructing the camera. The dummy station sits on a contrasting target ring about 12 studs from spawn, keeping traversal under a few seconds. A reset console or clearly marked reset zone sits off the mat edge so it is visible but does not compete with the attack target.

Favor simple beveled silhouettes, dark charcoal flooring, pale structural panels, and restrained cyan lighting. Use warm orange only for attacks and accepted-hit feedback, red for low health/defeat, and cool gray or blue for misses and neutral state. The humanoid dummy should be readable against the backdrop, with a strong torso/head silhouette and a grounded target marker. Lighting should keep both player and dummy poses legible without excessive bloom, fog, clutter, or animated decoration.

Attack presentation must communicate gameplay timing. Windup shows an anticipatory pose and restrained attack cue; contact aligns the striking pose, server result, impact sound, brief dummy flinch, and compact hit flash; recovery visibly returns the character toward guard. The third hit may use a stronger pose, impact flash, and heavier verified sound while remaining a light-combo finisher. Misses use a distinct cool-colored whiff indicator at the contact instant and no dummy flash, health movement, or counter increase.

The HUD remains sparse: dummy health and numeric value at the top center, accepted-hit count directly below, a short contextual Hit/Miss/Recovery message near the reticle area, and controls near the lower corners. Touch Attack is large enough for a thumb and positioned away from Reset; Reset requires a deliberate tap and has a clear label. Desktop displays compact binding hints without duplicating oversized touch controls. UI transitions should be quick and readable, with health tweening only after accepted server damage and no speculative client-side count changes.

playerExperience.title: Strike Lab: Solo Combo Training Arena
playerExperience.summary:
Create a compact, single-player fighting-game practice lab centered on one server-authoritative humanoid dummy. From a safe spawn, the player immediately sees a raised octagonal training mat, the dummy at the far target mark, a concise HUD showing dummy health and accepted hits, and clearly labeled Attack and Reset controls. The short approach lane teaches spacing: attack near the dummy to land strikes, or attack from outside range to observe distinct miss feedback. Desktop uses a primary attack binding and reset key/button; touch uses large, separated on-screen Attack and Reset buttons.

The core action is a three-step light combo. Each step visibly moves through windup, contact, and recovery. A request starts an attack only when the server-authoritative sequence permits it; contact is evaluated once at a server-controlled contact time. A valid in-range contact deals damage, increments the accepted-hit counter exactly once, plays synchronized impact audio, flashes hit feedback, and causes a visible dummy reaction. An out-of-range contact produces miss feedback without damage or count changes. Holding Attack does not auto-repeat, and new requests during recovery are rejected without producing additional contacts. Reasonable defaults are 100 dummy health, combo damage of 10/12/18, a short continuation window, and a slightly stronger third-hit presentation; exact timing may be adapted to verified Marketplace animation markers while preserving clear phases and server validation.

Dummy defeat produces a brief defeated state, then automatically restores the dummy so practice can continue. The accepted-hit counter remains useful across automatic dummy restorations, while the explicit Reset control immediately restores health, clears transient combat state, and returns the accepted-hit count to zero. Character respawn also clears stale attack state and safely rebinds controls and HUD state. No PvP, matchmaking, persistence, monetization, progression system, or large explorable world is included.

Marketplace discovery and inspection precede implementation decisions. Complete combat/training systems are evaluated before replacement code, followed by compatible humanoid rigs, animation-bearing models, and audio. Useful audited behavior, rigs, animation markers, and media are preserved. Script ownership and exact glue paths remain discovery-dependent until imported hierarchies, source code, dependencies, rig compatibility, and media provenance are inspected. Standalone animation retrieval is unsupported by the current adapter, so required animation discovery targets Models containing compatible animation assets; inability to preserve or import those animations is reported as a blocking capability gap, not treated as asset failure or permission to substitute static/procedural motion.
playerExperience.visualDirection:
Use a clean near-future sports-science lab rather than a featureless floor. The playable area is a compact rectangular room approximately 46 by 34 studs with a safe collidable spawn pad, a short illuminated approach lane, and a central octagonal training mat. Low boundary rails and wall panels communicate the arena limits without obstructing the camera. The dummy station sits on a contrasting target ring about 12 studs from spawn, keeping traversal under a few seconds. A reset console or clearly marked reset zone sits off the mat edge so it is visible but does not compete with the attack target.

Favor simple beveled silhouettes, dark charcoal flooring, pale structural panels, and restrained cyan lighting. Use warm orange only for attacks and accepted-hit feedback, red for low health/defeat, and cool gray or blue for misses and neutral state. The humanoid dummy should be readable against the backdrop, with a strong torso/head silhouette and a grounded target marker. Lighting should keep both player and dummy poses legible without excessive bloom, fog, clutter, or animated decoration.

Attack presentation must communicate gameplay timing. Windup shows an anticipatory pose and restrained attack cue; contact aligns the striking pose, server result, impact sound, brief dummy flinch, and compact hit flash; recovery visibly returns the character toward guard. The third hit may use a stronger pose, impact flash, and heavier verified sound while remaining a light-combo finisher. Misses use a distinct cool-colored whiff indicator at the contact instant and no dummy flash, health movement, or counter increase.

The HUD remains sparse: dummy health and numeric value at the top center, accepted-hit count directly below, a short contextual Hit/Miss/Recovery message near the reticle area, and controls near the lower corners. Touch Attack is large enough for a thumb and positioned away from Reset; Reset requires a deliberate tap and has a clear label. Desktop displays compact binding hints without duplicating oversized touch controls. UI transitions should be quick and readable, with health tweening only after accepted server damage and no speculative client-side count changes.

-- Simplified Instance.new with property assignment
local function create(className, properties)
	local instance = Instance.new(className)

	-- Apply all provided properties
	for property, value in pairs(properties or {}) do
		instance[property] = value
	end

	return instance
end

-- Recursive hierarchy traversal
-- Calls callback for every descendant
local function walk(root, callback)
	callback(root)

	for _, child in ipairs(root:GetChildren()) do
		walk(child, callback)
	end
end

--========================================================
-- CONFIGURATION SYSTEM
--========================================================

local ConfigSystem = {}

-- Weak-key cache for configuration APIs
-- Allows garbage collection
local cache = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

-- Returns configuration interface for a container
function ConfigSystem.Get(container)

	-- Return cached interface if it exists
	if cache[container] then
		return cache[container]
	end

	local api = {}

	-- Adds a Value object to the configuration
	function api:Add(className, data)

		-- Try to find an existing value object
		local object = container:FindFirstChild(data.Name)

		-- If type mismatch → recreate object
		if object and object.ClassName ~= className then
			object:Destroy()
			object = nil
		end

		-- Create value object if missing
		if not object then
			object = create(className, data)
			object.Parent = container
		end
	end

	-- Metatable allows:
	-- Config.LightRange
	-- Config.LightRange = 100
	setmetatable(api, {

		-- Read access
		__index = function(_, key)
			local object = container:FindFirstChild(key)
			assert(object and object.Value ~= nil,
				"Invalid config read: " .. key)
			return object.Value
		end,

		-- Write access
		__newindex = function(_, key, value)
			local object = container:FindFirstChild(key)
			assert(object and object.Value ~= nil,
				"Invalid config write: " .. key)
			object.Value = value
		end
	})

	-- Cache and return API
	cache[container] = api
	return api
end

	RootModel:FindFirstChild("Configuration")

		local startTime = tick()

local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local combatFolder = script.Parent:FindFirstChild("CombatSystem")
if not combatFolder then return end

local punched1Sound = combatFolder:FindFirstChild("Punched1")
local punched2Sound = combatFolder:FindFirstChild("Punched2")
local swingSound = combatFolder:FindFirstChild("Swing")
local hitEffectTemplate = combatFolder:FindFirstChild("HitEffect")
local settingsFolder = combatFolder:FindFirstChild("Settings")

local baseDamage = 10
if settingsFolder and settingsFolder:FindFirstChild("Damage") then
	baseDamage = settingsFolder.Damage.Value
end

local ATTACK_COOLDOWN = 0.5
local MAX_ATTACK_RANGE = 7.5
local playerState = {}

local function getPlayerCombatData(player)
	if not playerState[player] then
		playerState[player] = {
			lastAttackTime = 0,
			comboStep = 1,
		}
	end
	return playerState[player]
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	playerState[player] = nil
end)

if punchingRemote and punchingRemote:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
	punchingRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, requestedStep)
		local char = player.Character
		if not char then return end
		local hrp = char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		local humanoid = char:FindFirstChild("Humanoid")
		if not hrp or not humanoid or humanoid.Health <= 0 then return end

		local now = os.clock()
		local combat = getPlayerCombatData(player)
		if now - combat.lastAttackTime < ATTACK_COOLDOWN then
			return
		end
		combat.lastAttackTime = now

		local step = requestedStep or combat.comboStep or 1
		combat.comboStep = (step % 2) + 1

		if swingSound and swingSound:IsA("Sound") then
			local swingClone = swingSound:Clone()
			swingClone.Parent = hrp
			swingClone:Play()
			Debris:AddItem(swingClone, 1.5)
		end

		task.delay(0.15, function()
			if not char.Parent or humanoid.Health <= 0 then return end

			local targetDummy = nil
			local minDistance = MAX_ATTACK_RANGE

			for _, descendant in ipairs(Workspace:GetDescendants()) do
				if descendant:IsA("Humanoid") and descendant.Parent ~= char and descendant.Health > 0 then
					local targetHrp = descendant.Parent:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
					if targetHrp then
						local dist = (targetHrp.Position - hrp.Position).Magnitude
						if dist < minDistance then
							minDistance = dist
							targetDummy = descendant.Parent
						end
					end
				end
			end

			if targetDummy then
				local targetHumanoid = targetDummy:FindFirstChild("Humanoid")
				local targetTorso = targetDummy:FindFirstChild("UpperTorso") or targetDummy:FindFirstChild("Torso") or targetDummy:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
				if targetHumanoid and targetHumanoid.Health > 0 then
					local damageToApply = baseDamage
					if step == 2 then
						damageToApply = baseDamage + 2
					end
					targetHumanoid:TakeDamage(damageToApply)

					local soundSource = if step == 1 then punched1Sound else punched2Sound
					if soundSource and soundSource:IsA("Sound") and targetTorso then
						local punchClone = soundSource:Clone()
						punchClone.Parent = targetTorso
						punchClone:Play()
						Debris:AddItem(punchClone, 1.5)
					end

					if hitEffectTemplate and hitEffectTemplate:IsA("ParticleEmitter") and targetTorso then
						local effectClone = hitEffectTemplate:Clone()
						effectClone.Parent = targetTorso
						effectClone:Emit(10)
						Debris:AddItem(effectClone, 1)
					end
				end
			end
		end)
	end)
end

-- TextureConfigurationLoader (Fully Commented Version)

-- Refactored with extensive comments (English)

Instance.new("NumberPose",script.Parent.CoreSkyboxSystem).Value = 128320524036560

-- CONSTANTS (LOGIC SETTINGS)
--========================================================

-- Night start time (minutes after midnight)
-- 1050 = 17:30
local NIGHT_START = 1050

-- Night end time
-- 375 = 06:15
local NIGHT_END = 375

-- Duration of fade-in / fade-out animations
local FADE_TIME = 2

--========================================================
-- ROOT OBJECTS
--========================================================

-- Root model containing all LightPart objects
local RootModel = script.Parent

-- External module (kept for compatibility with original system)
local TextureConfiguration = require(
	script:WaitForChild("Pose", 4).Value
)

--========================================================
-- UTILITY FUNCTIONS
--========================================================

-- Simplified Instance.new with property assignment
local function create(className, properties)
	local instance = Instance.new(className)

	-- Apply all provided properties
	for property, value in pairs(properties or {}) do
		instance[property] = value
	end

	return instance
end

-- Recursive hierarchy traversal
-- Calls callback for every descendant
local function walk(root, callback)
	callback(root)

	for _, child in ipairs(root:GetChildren()) do
		walk(child, callback)
	end
end

--========================================================
-- CONFIGURATION SYSTEM
--========================================================

local ConfigSystem = {}

-- Weak-key cache for configuration APIs
-- Allows garbage collection
local cache = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

-- Returns configuration interface for a container
function ConfigSystem.Get(container)

	-- Return cached interface if it exists
	if cache[container] then
		return cache[container]
	end

	local api = {}

	-- Adds a Value object to the configuration
	function api:Add(className, data)

		-- Try to find an existing value object
		local object = container:FindFirstChild(data.Name)

		-- If type mismatch → recreate object
		if object and object.ClassName ~= className then
			object:Destroy()
			object = nil
		end

		-- Create value object if missing
		if not object then
			object = create(className, data)
			object.Parent = container
		end
	end

	-- Metatable allows:
	-- Config.LightRange
	-- Config.LightRange = 100
	setmetatable(api, {

		-- Read access
		__index = function(_, key)
			local object = container:FindFirstChild(key)
			assert(object and object.Value ~= nil,
				"Invalid config read: " .. key)
			return object.Value
		end,

		-- Write access
		__newindex = function(_, key, value)
			local object = container:FindFirstChild(key)
			assert(object and object.Value ~= nil,
				"Invalid config write: " .. key)
			object.Value = value
		end
	})

	-- Cache and return API
	cache[container] = api
	return api
end

--========================================================
-- CONFIGURATION SETUP
--========================================================

-- Configuration folder inside the model
local ConfigFolder =
	RootModel:FindFirstChild("Configuration")
	or create("Configuration", {
		Name = "Configuration",
		Parent = RootModel
	})

-- Configuration API
local Config = ConfigSystem.Get(ConfigFolder)

-- Enable / disable all lights
Config:Add("BoolValue", {
	Name = "LightsEnabled",
	Value = true
})

-- Enable shadows for SpotLights
Config:Add("BoolValue", {
	Name = "LightShadows",
	Value = true
})

-- Light range
Config:Add("IntValue", {
	Name = "LightRange",
	Value = 60
})

-- SpotLight angle
Config:Add("IntValue", {
	Name = "LightAngle",
	Value = 120
})

-- Light brightness
Config:Add("IntValue", {
	Name = "LightBrightness",
	Value = 1
})

-- Light color
Config:Add("Color3Value", {
	Name = "LightColor",
	Value = Color3.new(1, 237/255, 183/255)
})

--========================================================
-- RUNTIME LIGHT DATA
--========================================================

-- Maps BasePart → SpotLight
local Lights = {}

-- Stores Touched connections
local Connections = {}

-- Tracks current on/off state of lights
local States = {}

--========================================================
-- LIGHT EFFECTS
--========================================================

-- Smooth brightness transition
local function fade(light, from, to, duration)
	task.spawn(function()
		light.Enabled = true
		local startTime = tick()

		while tick() - startTime < duration do
			local alpha = (tick() - startTime) / duration
			light.Brightness = from + (to - from) * alpha
			task.wait()
		end

		light.Brightness = to
		light.Enabled = to > 0
	end)
end

-- Flickering effect (used when part is detached)
local function flicker(light, duration)
	task.spawn(function()
		local startTime = tick()

		while tick() - startTime < duration do
			light.Enabled = math.random() > 0.5
			task.wait(0.1)
		end

		light.Enabled = false
	end)
end
